stem: A 23 year old man is involved in a road traffic collision and sustains a lumbar fracture. On examination you note he is unable to extend his big toe. Which of the following spinal nerve roots has most likely been affected:
fact: L5 root involvement impairs great-toe extension.
finding: Source key and standard myotome anatomy support L5.

stem: The two cerebral hemispheres are connected by which of the following structures:
fact: The corpus callosum is the major commissural white-matter connection between cerebral hemispheres.

stem: The Wernicke's speech area is located in which of the following regions:
fact: Wernicke area is located in the dominant temporal lobe and supports language comprehension.
mnemonic: Wernicke works with words in the temporal lobe.

stem: A 55 year old woman presents to ED complaining of headaches. On examination the patient is found to have weakness of the left side of her body and her eyes are deviated towards the right hand side. The lesion is most likely to be in the:
fact: A right frontal lesion can cause left-sided weakness and gaze deviation toward the lesion through motor-cortex and frontal-eye-field involvement.
mnemonic: Frontal field and motor power point the eyes and body toward the lesion.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical cerebellar sign:
fact: Cerebellar dysfunction is associated with hypotonia, not hypertonia, as well as dysdiadochokinesia, nystagmus, intention tremor, and scanning speech.
mnemonic: Cerebellum: low tone, shaky target, poor rapid alternation.
finding: Source explanation identifies hypertonia as the exception.

stem: Damage to Wernicke's area will most likely result in which of the following clinical features:
fact: Dominant Wernicke-area injury causes receptive dysphasia with impaired comprehension.

stem: Which of the following blood vessels is NOT part of the circle of Willis:
fact: The middle cerebral artery is a lateral continuation of the internal carotid and is not part of the arterial circle of Willis.
mnemonic: MCA moves laterally outside the circle.
finding: NCBI optic-tract anatomy supports the circle components and the MCA exception.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical cause of a bitemporal hemianopia:
options: Aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery
fact: Bitemporal hemianopia reflects optic-chiasm compression; posterior cerebral artery stroke more typically causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia.
mnemonic: Chiasm compression cuts temporal fields; PCA cuts one side of both fields.

stem: Which of the following spinal tracts is involved with the control of trunk muscles:
fact: The anterior corticospinal tract contributes to control of trunk and axial muscles.

stem: Occlusion of which of the following blood vessels is most likely to result in a receptive dysphasia:
fact: Dominant superior temporal Wernicke-area language cortex is supplied by the middle cerebral artery; occlusion can cause receptive dysphasia.
finding: NCBI aphasia and Wernicke pages support the displayed key.
